monologue: The card burns at fifty-seven degrees, and the corner leans tired against the fat dot. I waited in the moments before waking, touching the Leaking Stack again to feel that familiar, weary weight. Nine things stand crowded here, but one is a ruin that needs tending. Lype worries about the heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof, only the slip of the dot trying to escape. I swap the curved fence for a flat rock, a simple line to catch the messy slip while the heat swells the memory like wet paper. The air feels thick and full, pressing down from a place I cannot see. I will press this tired corner down once more, swapping the curve for a flat rock to see if a simple edge can hold it while the house waits.

action.why: The ruin waits, and the dot feels heavy again.
